project.name: Chronobreak
project.description: Canonical Chronobreak roadmap reconciled from repository implementation, product boundaries, specifications, and verification evidence.

features.name: Capture Reliability
features.description: Make automatic recording trustworthy enough that Chronobreak does not silently lose or corrupt the game the user expected it to preserve.
evidence: QB-CAP-001 provides the existing process-driven lifecycle and interrupted fragmented-MP4 baseline; health monitoring, recovery tooling, integrity validation, and storage preflight remain open.
success_criteria: Known capture failure modes are converted into concrete child features with deterministic detection/recovery behavior.
Chronobreak does not silently report a failed/frozen recording as healthy.
Recoverable interruptions preserve as much valid footage as practical.
Reliability claims are backed by explicit failure-injection or integrity verification.
features.notes: This is intentionally an epic, not an executable 'optimize reliability' feature.

features.name: Automatic Match Recording Lifecycle
features.description: Automatically detect a League match, start recording, stop/finalize at match end, and associate the recording with the correct match.
evidence: recorder/src/service.rs and recorder/src/watcher.rs implement League-process appearance, replacement, disappearance, and shutdown transitions around one active ffmpeg session.
recorder/src/encoder.rs writes fragmented MP4 and preserves partial output on an unexpected encoder exit; recorder/src/poller.rs writes final match metadata tied to the same game directory.
PHASES.md records explicit Phase 1 live validation for completed and interrupted games; recorder automated tests and format check passed on 2026-08-11.
acceptance_criteria: A configured League match starts recording without manual user action.
Recording finalizes when the match ends.
The finalized recording is associated with the correct match.
Unexpected League termination leaves Chronobreak in a recoverable/known state.

verification.description: Verify lifecycle/state transitions where testable.
Run an end-to-end match lifecycle against the supported test environment.

features.notes: Existing shipped baseline. Full output-progress health monitoring and post-finalization integrity checks are intentionally separate features.

features.name: Recording Health Monitoring
features.description: Detect whether active recording output is actually progressing rather than assuming a running recorder process means healthy capture.
acceptance_criteria: Chronobreak can distinguish healthy progressing output from a stalled/failed capture condition.
A detected unhealthy state is surfaced clearly and is not silently reported as success.
Healthy recordings do not generate unacceptable false failure indications.

verification.description: Inject or simulate stalled/failing output conditions where feasible.
Verify the health signal is based on meaningful output progress/encoder state.

features.notes: Current code checks ffmpeg process liveness only; this feature must define and test meaningful output-progress signals and false-positive bounds.

features.name: Interrupted Recording Recovery
features.description: Recover as much valid footage as practical after an interrupted or ungracefully finalized recording.
acceptance_criteria: An intentionally interrupted recording can be recovered to a playable file when the chosen media/container strategy permits it.
Recovery does not duplicate the match in the library.
Unrecoverable cases are reported explicitly.

verification.description: Interrupt a fixture recording before graceful finalization and exercise recovery.
Open and seek through recovered output.

features.notes: Fragmented MP4 currently preserves completed fragments, but there is no discovery/repair workflow or explicit unrecoverable-state reporting.

features.name: Post-recording Integrity Verification
features.description: Validate finalized recordings cheaply enough to detect obviously broken, malformed, frozen, or missing-stream output.
acceptance_criteria: Chronobreak validates expected media streams and sensible duration/timestamps after finalization.
Known malformed fixture output is detected.
A valid recording passes without unnecessary user-facing noise.

verification.description: Validate good and deliberately malformed media fixtures.

features.notes: The app validates selected metadata before playback/export, but recorder finalization does not currently run ffprobe or a content-progress integrity check.

features.name: Storage Preflight for Recording
features.description: Prevent avoidable recording failure caused by insufficient available storage before or during a match.
acceptance_criteria: Chronobreak checks whether recording storage is critically constrained before starting capture.
The user receives a clear actionable state when recording cannot safely start.
Storage checks do not destructively delete protected media.

verification.description: Exercise preflight against controlled low-space/limit conditions where feasible.
Verify user-facing failure behavior.

features.notes: Post-game usage and age retention exist in the app; the recorder does not currently check free space before or during capture.

features.name: Negligible Capture Performance Impact
features.description: Make automatic Chronobreak capture cheap enough that competitive League players can leave it enabled by default.
success_criteria: A reproducible benchmark protocol and performance budget exist.
Capture performance is measured using metrics relevant to game responsiveness, not only average resource usage.
Concrete optimization work is created from measured regressions/bottlenecks rather than vague 'make it faster' tasks.
features.notes: Do not implement this epic directly. First establish benchmark/budget, then create measured optimization features.

features.name: Capture Benchmark and Performance Budget
features.description: Define and automate/reproduce the benchmark used to measure Chronobreak capture overhead and the budget required before performance claims can be made.
acceptance_criteria: The benchmark scenario is documented and repeatable.
The benchmark records the project-selected FPS/frametime and system/encoder metrics.
A baseline without Chronobreak capture and a Chronobreak-enabled run can be compared.
An explicit acceptable performance budget is documented before optimization features are declared complete.

verification.description: Run the documented baseline and Chronobreak capture benchmark.
Verify methodology and result storage are reproducible.

features.notes: Recorder diagnostics has a short synthetic encoder-selection benchmark, but the required baseline-versus-capture League FPS/frametime protocol and budget do not exist.

features.name: League-native Replay Experience
features.description: Make Chronobreak feel like a playable League match history rather than a generic video player.
evidence: Synchronized match data, the primary event timeline, state-at-playhead, byte-range playback, and Data Dragon presentation exist; category lanes, hover thumbnails, and broader navigation remain open.
success_criteria: Video, game events, and recorded match state share a reliable timeline.
Important moments are fast to locate and seek.
Replay navigation remains responsive on long/event-heavy matches.
Replay UI exposes descriptive game context without becoming coaching.

features.name: Synchronized League Match Data
features.description: Persist League Live Client Data and timestamped events against a common match clock usable by replay features.
evidence: recorder/src/poller.rs implements monotonic clock calibration, cumulative event deduplication, concurrent snapshots, derived item/level changes, and precomputed video_time_ms.
recorder/src/storage.rs atomically replaces game_log.json; unavailable fields remain optional rather than inferred.
PHASES.md records explicit Phase 2 synchronization validation; recorder automated tests and format check passed on 2026-08-11.
acceptance_criteria: Persisted events retain usable timestamps.
Required match/player metadata is stored for replay/search features.
Video time and game-data time can be mapped consistently across a complete match.
Missing snapshots/data are represented as missing rather than invented.

verification.description: Use deterministic fixtures to test time mapping and stored event/state retrieval.
Check synchronization at multiple timestamps in a representative recording.

features.notes: Existing shipped baseline. The Live Client API can disappear independently; video capture continues and unavailable fields remain missing.

features.name: League-native Timeline Interaction
features.description: Provide a polished timeline that exposes League events clearly and supports precise seeking without becoming visually unreadable.
evidence: app/src/components/ViewerScreen.tsx renders sorted video_time_ms markers, click/keyboard seeking, dense marker presentation, and shared windowed/fullscreen state.
app/src-tauri/src/library.rs builds sorted frame-driven playback payloads and tests mandatory frame-rate metadata.
PHASES.md records explicit Phase 4 and 5 validation on representative recordings; Tauri tests, Clippy, frontend type-check, and frontend build passed on 2026-08-11.
acceptance_criteria: Supported event markers align with their replay timestamps.
Dense event periods remain usable.
Selecting an event seeks accurately.
Timeline interaction remains responsive on representative long matches.

verification.description: Test event-to-timestamp mapping and seek requests where feasible.
Review usability on sparse and event-heavy matches.

features.notes: Existing primary timeline baseline. Category-specific lanes and hover previews remain separate features.

features.name: Timeline Event Lanes and Filters
features.description: Allow users to focus the replay timeline on event categories such as kills, deaths, objectives, bookmarks, and clips.
evidence: The current viewer supports participant-based event filtering, but it does not expose independent event-category lanes/filters or bookmark/clip lanes.
acceptance_criteria: Supported event categories can be shown/hidden without changing timestamps.
Filtering reduces clutter on event-heavy matches.
The default presentation remains understandable without configuration.

verification.description: Verify filtering preserves underlying event data/timestamps.
Review dense-match usability.

features.notes: Extend the existing marker/filter model; participant filtering is supporting evidence, not completion of category filtering.

features.name: Timeline Hover Thumbnails
features.description: Show a preview frame for the timestamp under the cursor while hovering/scrubbing the replay timeline.
acceptance_criteria: The thumbnail corresponds closely to the hovered timestamp.
Repeated hover previews are responsive.
Thumbnail generation/retrieval does not cause unacceptable playback stalls.
Long recordings do not create uncontrolled cache/storage growth.

verification.description: Test timestamp-to-thumbnail lookup and cache behavior where feasible.
Scrub representative short and long recordings.
Measure hover/preview latency if infrastructure supports it.

features.notes: No hover-frame extraction or cache exists. Design must preserve the single-video playback hot path and bound generated cache growth.

features.name: State at Playhead
features.description: Update descriptive match/player state in the replay UI according to the current video timestamp.
evidence: app/src/viewerUtils.ts performs binary-search timeline lookup and app/src/components/ViewerScreen.tsx renders recorded champion, KDA, CS, level, and item state from the presented-frame clock.
APP-VIEWER.md explicitly limits the surface to available descriptive data and records backward-seek behavior.
PHASES.md records Phase 4 validation; Tauri tests and frontend type-check passed on 2026-08-11.
acceptance_criteria: Seeking to known timestamps displays the corresponding available recorded state.
Seeking backward restores earlier state correctly.
Missing data is not fabricated.
The feature remains descriptive and does not judge player decisions.

verification.description: Use fixtures with known snapshots to test state lookup.
Seek through a representative recording and compare state to known events.

features.notes: Existing shipped baseline; no coaching or inferred unavailable state is part of this feature.

features.name: Replay Navigation Shortcuts
features.description: Provide fast keyboard navigation for common replay operations such as seeking and moving between events.
acceptance_criteria: Documented shortcuts perform their intended replay actions.
Shortcuts do not conflict unexpectedly with focused text/input controls.
Navigation remains consistent with timeline state.

verification.description: Exercise each shortcut in the replay viewer.
Test shortcut-to-action mapping where the UI test stack allows it.

features.notes: The scrubber and clip endpoints already have focused keyboard behavior; this item covers documented viewer-wide navigation and event traversal.

features.name: Playable Match and Clip Library
features.description: Make recorded games and clips searchable, linked, portable, and organized using League semantics rather than opaque filenames.
evidence: Filesystem-derived game/clip browsing, source-derived clip presentation, usage reporting, save protection, and age retention exist; semantic search, durable clip event metadata, relocation, import, and sessions remain open.
success_criteria: Matches are queryable by useful League metadata.
Clips preserve their relationship to source matches and contained events.
Library state can be recovered/re-indexed without making one opaque database the sole authority.
Storage growth remains manageable.

features.name: Searchable Match History
features.description: Search/filter recorded matches using League metadata such as champion, enemy champions, queue/mode, result, participants, and recorded events.
evidence: The current library derives champion, mode, participants/loadout, and KDA-related summary data from bundle metadata, but exposes no search/filter UI or persisted search index.
acceptance_criteria: Search by played champion returns only matching recorded matches.
Search by enemy champion and supported event returns matching recorded matches.
Multiple supported filters can be combined.
Search operates on persisted indexed metadata rather than filenames alone.

verification.description: Use deterministic library fixtures to verify each supported query and combined filters.
Exercise search/filter UI with a populated test library.

features.notes: Keep draft until supported filters are reconciled with local-data limits: the current recorder cannot truthfully infer match result, and enemy/participant availability must be defined for incomplete bundles.

features.name: Clip Metadata and Event Tagging
features.description: Derive clip metadata from the source match and attach only timestamped events that occur within the clip interval.
acceptance_criteria: A clip inherits relevant source-match metadata.
Only events whose timestamps fall within the clip range are attached.
Clip metadata is queryable by the same relevant library search mechanisms.

verification.description: Create fixture clips whose ranges include/exclude known events and verify tags.

features.notes: Current clip filenames link to a source game and the library derives source champion/date at scan time, but no clip metadata sidecar persists the selected range or in-range event tags for search.

features.name: Source Match and Clip Linking
features.description: Persist the relationship between a Chronobreak-created clip and its source match/time range.
acceptance_criteria: A match exposes clips created from it.
A clip can navigate back to its source replay at the expected timestamp.
Deleting a clip does not delete the source match.

verification.description: Create multiple clips from a fixture match and verify relationships.
Navigate match -> clip and clip -> source replay.

features.notes: Current clip names/summaries retain source game identity, but match-to-clips and clip-to-source-at-time navigation are not both exposed in the UI.

features.name: Storage Budget and Retention
features.description: Let users set a maximum Chronobreak recording budget, understand remaining capacity, and safely reclaim eligible old recordings.
evidence: app/src-tauri/src/library.rs already reports game-video and clip-MP4 usage and implements tested age-based cleanup that skips saved and incomplete games; no maximum-byte budget or remaining-hours model exists.
acceptance_criteria: Current Chronobreak-managed media usage is reported accurately enough for user decisions.
A configured maximum storage budget persists.
Estimated remaining recording capacity uses a documented model.
Automatic cleanup never deletes protected items.
Cleanup behavior is deterministic and explainable.

verification.description: Test budget calculation and retention selection against fixture libraries.
Verify settings/usage/remaining-capacity UI.
Verify destructive tests only operate on designated test data.

features.notes: Build on the narrower completed age-retention baseline without weakening saved/incomplete-item protection.

features.name: Portable Re-indexable Chronobreak Library
features.description: Make Chronobreak-created media relationships reconstructable after index loss or library relocation using durable metadata.
acceptance_criteria: A test library can be re-indexed after removing/rebuilding disposable index state.
Matches regain durable metadata required by supported features.
Source-match/clip relationships survive reconstruction.
Relocating the library does not permanently orphan valid Chronobreak media.

verification.description: Build, discard index state, then reconstruct a fixture library.
Relocate a test library and verify re-link/re-index behavior.

features.notes: In-place app restarts already rescan bundles without a database; relocation and reconstruction of every durable relationship are not yet proved.

features.name: Gaming Session Grouping
features.description: Group temporally adjacent matches into browsing sessions while keeping individual matches independently accessible.
acceptance_criteria: Matches separated by less than the configured/defined threshold group into one session.
A sufficiently long break creates a new session.
Session grouping does not alter underlying match metadata.

verification.description: Test grouping against deterministic timestamp fixtures.
Review session grouping in match-history UI.

features.notes: Keep draft until the session-gap threshold and whether it is fixed or user-configurable are deliberately defined.

features.name: Import and Relink Existing Recordings
features.description: Rediscover moved Chronobreak recordings and provide a safe path for importing compatible external videos with reduced metadata where necessary.
success_criteria: Moved Chronobreak libraries can be relinked without corrupting durable bundle relationships.
Compatible external videos can be imported with an explicit reduced-metadata identity.
Unsupported or metadata-poor media never pretends to contain unavailable League events.
features.notes: The seed combined relocation recovery and external-video ingestion. They have different ownership, metadata, and failure semantics and are decomposed into QB-LIB-010 and QB-LIB-011.

features.name: Relink a Moved Chronobreak Library
features.description: Point Chronobreak at a relocated library of existing game bundles and clips and reconstruct supported relationships without rewriting valid source media.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a relocated valid Chronobreak root rediscovers its game and clip entries.
Durable match/clip relationships and supported metadata survive relocation.
Relinking does not copy, delete, or rewrite valid source media merely to make it visible.
Missing files, duplicate identities, and incompatible bundles are reported explicitly without corrupting the test library.

verification.description: Relocate controlled fixture libraries and verify reconstruction, conflicts, and source hashes.
Move a dedicated test library, select the new root, and browse/play its restored entries.

features.notes: Use only dedicated fixture/test libraries for relocation and conflict tests.

features.name: Import External Video as Reduced-metadata Replay
features.description: Add a compatible external video to the library with an explicit reduced-metadata identity and no fabricated League timeline data.
acceptance_criteria: A supported external video can be added with a visibly reduced-metadata identity.
Imported media never claims unavailable League participants, events, snapshots, or source-match relationships.
Unsupported or malformed media fails explicitly without leaving a false complete library entry.
The chosen copy-versus-reference ownership policy is visible and preserves the original input.

verification.description: Import supported, unsupported, missing, and malformed fixture media and verify reduced metadata and cleanup behavior.
Import and play representative test media and verify the reduced-metadata UI and ownership behavior.

features.notes: Keep draft until supported containers/codecs and whether Chronobreak copies or references imported files are deliberate product decisions.

features.name: Fast League-native Clipping
features.description: Make the path from an indexed League event or remembered moment to a usable MP4 exceptionally fast and simple.
evidence: Event-to-clip activation and compatible preset export exist; deterministic event clustering, guaranteed multikill boundaries, remux/copy optimization, and montage generation remain open.
success_criteria: Users can create clips directly from meaningful replay moments.
Chronobreak uses event knowledge to reduce manual endpoint work.
Export is reliable, compatible, and avoids unnecessary processing.

features.name: Smart Event Clustering
features.description: Group temporally related game events into coherent replay moments that can drive timeline display and clip boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: Known multikill sequences cluster deterministically.
Unrelated temporally separated events are not incorrectly merged.
Cluster start/end timestamps are stable and reusable by clipping.

verification.description: Run deterministic event-clustering fixtures for single/multi-event sequences.

features.notes: Current clip defaults inspect nearby Multikill telemetry but do not persist deterministic reusable clusters with explicit start/end timestamps.

features.name: Smart Clip Boundaries
features.description: Pre-position clip endpoints around the full relevant event sequence, especially multikills, while keeping endpoints editable.
evidence: app/src/viewerUtils.ts supplies editable frame-aligned single-event and multikill-aware heuristic ranges, but it does not prove that first-through-final events of every supported multikill cluster are enclosed.
acceptance_criteria: Creating a clip from a supported multikill includes setup before the first relevant kill and aftermath after the final kill.
The entire multikill sequence lies inside the initial range.
Automatically selected endpoints remain manually adjustable.
Single-event clipping remains supported.

verification.description: Test boundary calculation against event fixtures.
Create clips from known single-kill and multikill recordings.

features.notes: The existing heuristic is a partial baseline. Completion requires deterministic cluster-derived boundaries and fixtures proving full-sequence inclusion.

features.name: Instant Event-to-Clip Action
features.description: Create a clip directly from a replay event using the event/cluster as initial context.
evidence: app/src/components/ViewerScreen.tsx exposes clip activation from supported replay events and carries the source timestamp into editable clip mode.
app/src/viewerUtils.ts applies available event-aware pre/post-roll heuristics and frame alignment.
PHASES.md records explicit Phase 7 end-to-end clip validation; frontend type-check and build passed on 2026-08-11.
acceptance_criteria: A supported event exposes a Create Clip action.
The action enters clip mode at the correct source moment.
Smart boundaries are applied when available.

verification.description: Test event action wiring where feasible.
Create clips directly from representative event markers.

features.notes: Existing event-action baseline. Deterministic clustering and guaranteed full multikill boundaries remain QB-CLIP-001 and QB-CLIP-002.

features.name: Fast Compatible MP4 Export
features.description: Export adjusted replay ranges to broadly compatible MP4 while avoiding unnecessary transcoding when the media pipeline permits it.
evidence: The completed preset exporter always creates compatible H.264/AAC output with hardware/software fallback and preserves sources; it does not currently use stream copy/remux when compatible.
acceptance_criteria: Exported clips open in the project-defined compatibility targets.
Audio/video remain synchronized.
Source recordings are never modified.
The export path avoids unnecessary re-encoding when correctness/compatibility allow it.

verification.description: Validate exported media structure with project media tooling.
Open representative exports in defined target players/apps.
Measure representative export latency once methodology is defined.

features.notes: Keep draft until compatibility targets and the safe stream-copy/remux decision matrix are explicit; the existing re-encoding exporter remains QB-CLIP-007.

features.name: Automatic Kill Montage
features.description: Generate one montage containing the selected player's kill sequences using indexed events and smart boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: All expected selected-player kill sequences from a fixture match are included.
Multikill sequences are not redundantly split into separate overlapping clips.
Unrelated footage is excluded except configured pre/post context.
Final montage is playable and synchronized.

verification.description: Generate montage from deterministic event fixture/recording.
Review ordering, boundaries, and final media.

features.notes: No montage pipeline exists; reuse cluster selection and the proven atomic export/media-validation path.

features.name: Automatic Game Highlights Recap
features.description: Generate a deterministic recap from supported recorded events/bookmarks without subjective coaching analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Highlight-selection rules are explicit and deterministic before implementation.
Every included segment maps to a supported recorded event/bookmark rule.
Adjacent related events are not redundantly duplicated.
The recap does not judge gameplay quality or provide coaching.

verification.description: Verify selection rules against representative event fixtures.
Review recap output from representative matches.

features.notes: Keep draft until highlight-selection rules are deliberately defined; this is intentionally late.

features.name: Local Byte-range Replay Playback
features.description: Stream large local recordings and clips to the Tauri webview with standards-compliant byte ranges so native video playback and seeking do not load whole media files into application memory.
evidence: app/src-tauri/src/playback_server.rs binds an ephemeral IPv4 loopback origin, validates media identifiers, serves single byte ranges, streams file slices, and records request/byte/completion metrics.
app/src/components/ViewerScreen.tsx keeps one native video element and uses presented-frame callbacks and serialized seeks rather than decoding or copying video in JavaScript.
PHASES.md records explicit large-recording browse/seek validation; playback-server tests, Tauri tests, and frontend checks passed on 2026-08-11.
acceptance_criteria: Recordings and clips support native webview playback and seeking through a loopback-only URL.
A range request streams only the requested file interval and does not load the whole recording into memory.
Unrecognized or traversal-like identifiers cannot escape configured media roots.
Playback diagnostics expose range/byte/stream counters without interrupting playback.

verification.description: Exercise range parsing, streamed-byte accounting, path validation, and playback payload construction.
Rapidly seek representative multi-gigabyte H.264 and supported HEVC recordings in the Tauri webview and inspect diagnostics.

features.notes: Existing shipped foundation used by the viewer, clip preview, music preview, and static-asset delivery.

features.name: Versioned Data Dragon Asset Cache
features.description: Resolve League champion and item presentation through a versioned local Data Dragon cache that remains non-blocking when the network or CDN is unavailable.
evidence: app/src-tauri/src/ddragon.rs initializes versioned manifests, resolves item names, validates PNG assets, and keeps cached versions usable on refresh failure.
app/src-tauri/src/playback_server.rs serves cached/missing Data Dragon assets through the loopback origin; the SolidJS library/viewer retain fixed placeholders on failure.
Data Dragon unit tests, Tauri tests, and frontend checks passed on 2026-08-11; PHASES.md records the cache as delivered in Phase 3.
acceptance_criteria: Champion and item names/icons resolve from a patch-versioned local cache.
Cached manifests and assets remain usable when refresh is unavailable.
Invalid or unavailable assets degrade to stable placeholders and never block library or replay playback.

verification.description: Exercise manifest parsing, item lookup, cache fallback, and safe asset resolution.
Open a representative library online and offline and verify cached assets/placeholders do not change layout or block playback.

features.notes: Existing shipped presentation foundation; static assets are a disposable cache, not canonical match data.

features.name: Filesystem-derived Game and Clip Library
features.description: Build the local Games and Clips library directly from ordinary recording bundles and clip artifacts without an opaque database.
evidence: app/src-tauri/src/library.rs scans games and clips, derives summaries from metadata/game logs, marks incomplete bundles conservatively, and validates identifiers before mutation.
app/src/App.tsx and app/src/components/LibraryScreen.tsx expose Games and Clips tabs, playback entry, save/delete actions, and explicit incomplete states.
Library fixture tests, Tauri tests, and frontend checks passed on 2026-08-11; PHASES.md records Phase 3 browse/play validation.
acceptance_criteria: Restarting the app rebuilds Games and Clips views by scanning the configured filesystem root without database state.
Valid game bundles expose League-aware summaries and playback entry; valid clip artifacts expose preview/library entries.
Incomplete or malformed bundles are represented conservatively rather than silently treated as complete.
Library mutations are restricted to validated managed entries.

verification.description: Scan fixture bundles and verify summaries, ordering, incomplete states, save/delete guards, and clip discovery.
Browse and open representative games/clips from a dedicated test library, restart the app, and verify the same entries are rediscovered.

features.notes: Existing local-first foundation. Relocation, external import, semantic search, and complete relationship reconstruction remain separate features.

features.name: Age-based Retention and Save Protection
features.description: Report game-video and clip-MP4 storage use and safely remove eligible recordings older than the configured retention period while preserving saved and incomplete games.
evidence: app/src-tauri/src/library.rs implements storage_usage, atomic saved-state updates, guarded deletion, and deterministic age-based run_auto_delete.
The auto-delete fixture test proves old eligible deletion while saved, recent, and incomplete games survive.
Tauri tests and frontend checks passed on 2026-08-11; APP-LIBRARY.md documents the settings/storage controls.
acceptance_criteria: Game-video and clip-MP4 byte usage and counts are available to the UI.
The retention-days setting persists and zero disables automatic age cleanup.
Cleanup deletes only complete, unsaved games older than the threshold.
Saved, recent, and incomplete games survive cleanup, and destructive tests use temporary libraries.

verification.description: Verify usage, saved-state preservation, deletion guards, and retention selection in temporary fixture libraries.
Use a dedicated test library to verify usage, save/unsave, retention settings, and cleanup feedback.

features.notes: Existing narrower baseline for QB-LIB-004; there is no maximum-byte budget or remaining-recording-capacity estimate yet.

features.name: Publishable H.264/AAC Preset Export
features.description: Export an adjusted replay range as atomic, source-preserving H.264/AAC MP4 outputs for Discord, horizontal, and vertical publishing presets.
evidence: app/src-tauri/src/clip_export.rs validates frame-aware ranges, encodes H.264/AAC with hardware preference/software fallback, enforces the Discord byte limit, stages batches, and generates paired thumbnails without modifying sources.
app/src/components/ClipExporterScreen.tsx implements preset selection, progress, retryable errors, and post-export actions.
PHASES.md records explicit H.264/HEVC-source export validation at phase-7; clip-export/Tauri tests and frontend checks passed on 2026-08-11.
acceptance_criteria: A valid selected range exports playable H.264/AAC MP4 for each requested Discord, horizontal, or vertical preset.
Discord output is verified below 10,000,000 bytes and retries correction before failing explicitly.
The source recording is never modified, and a failed batch does not expose partial outputs as completed clips.
Successful outputs use the source-linked filename contract, include thumbnail artifacts, and preserve audio/video synchronization.

verification.description: Exercise request/profile/filter/encoder argument generation, validation, and atomic path rules.
Export all presets from representative H.264 and HEVC fixtures, inspect with ffprobe, play them in compatibility targets, and verify source hashes are unchanged.

features.notes: Existing shipped re-encoding baseline. Conditional stream-copy/remux optimization remains QB-CLIP-004.

features.name: Self-contained Windows Beta
features.description: Ship the proven local record-to-clip workflow on Windows without requiring users to install ffmpeg, Rust, Node.js, or developer tooling.
success_criteria: A clean supported Windows machine can install Chronobreak and run the complete record, browse, replay, and export workflow with packaged dependencies.
Exactly one background recorder instance follows the user's login-startup setting without a console window.
Upgrade and uninstall preserve user recordings and remove only application-owned binaries and startup registration.
Bundled third-party tools and assets include required notices and licenses.
features.notes: Reconciled from the unimplemented Phase 8 scope in PHASES.md. Public signing, updates, and macOS distribution require later refinement and are not implied by this beta epic.

features.name: Packaged Media Tool Contract
features.description: Bundle ffmpeg and ffprobe as Windows application resources and give recorder diagnostics, capture, probing, thumbnailing, and clip export one explicit installed-tool discovery contract.
evidence: Current recorder development discovery supports an adjacent resources/ffmpeg candidate, while app export and library probing still invoke ffmpeg/ffprobe from PATH.
acceptance_criteria: The Windows package contains the required ffmpeg and ffprobe executables and applicable notices/licenses.
Recorder diagnostics/capture and app probing/export resolve the same packaged tool location in an installed build.
The installed workflow succeeds when no system ffmpeg or ffprobe is on PATH.
Missing, blocked, or incompatible packaged tools produce concise actionable errors.

verification.description: Test shared tool-path resolution and missing/incompatible-tool errors with controlled resource layouts.
Run diagnostics, record, probe, and export from an installed build on Windows without system media tools.
Verify packaged binaries and third-party notices are included in the release artifact.

features.notes: Cross-process packaging and media integrity make this planned work.

features.name: Single Recorder Supervision and Login Startup
features.description: Start and maintain exactly one installed background recorder instance, with a user-controlled Windows login-startup registration and no visible console window.
evidence: The recorder already supports tray/headless lifecycle and hides release console windows, but the app does not supervise an installed recorder or own login registration.
acceptance_criteria: Launching the installed app or logging in when enabled results in exactly one recorder process.
Repeated app launches and login triggers do not create duplicate recorders.
The recorder remains unobtrusive with tray state and no console window and can finalize an active recording on intentional shutdown.
Disabling login startup removes Chronobreak's registration without affecting recordings.

verification.description: Test single-instance/supervision state transitions and registration serialization where feasible.
